Soil observations: one row per horizon or per observation

Source: R/observations.R
soil_observations.Rd

Reads the measurements of a selection from the canonical layer of the Global Soil Data Hub (POST /query/observations, always canonical = true), page by page, and returns them as a typed table: with layout = "wide" (the default) one row per horizon and one group of columns per soil variable; with layout = "long" one row per observation (one measured value).

Usage

soil_observations(
  soil = soil_session(),
  datasets = NULL,
  variables = NULL,
  bbox = NULL,
  country = NULL,
  geometry = "any",
  layer = "all",
  view = "raw",
  profile_type = NULL,
  components = NULL,
  min_cumulative_percent = NULL,
  layout = c("wide", "long"),
  with_geometry = c("none", "sf", "text"),
  max_rows = Inf,
  offset = 0,
  page_size = NULL,
  too_large = c("stop", "export"),
  progress = interactive(),
  timeout = NULL
)

Arguments

soil

A session; the default session when omitted. Client-side: not sent to the API.

datasets

Catalog dataset codes ("wosis_points", "wise_profiles", "soter_profiles", "soter_polygons", "sotwis_polygons", "sotwis_components", "sotwis_estimates", see soil_datasets()); NULL (the API default) selects every dataset, usually above the limit of synchronous reads. API field datasets.

variables

Source codes ("ORGC", "CLAY") or canonical property keys ("organic_carbon"), see soil_variables(); NULL returns every variable. With variables the column set is fixed by the request, so every page has the same columns. API field variables.

bbox

c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in WGS84 degrees (longitude, latitude). API field bbox.

country

Countries as ISO 3166 alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes or names, case-insensitive (the API resolves them). API field country.

geometry

"any", "point" (profiles) or "polygon" (map units). API field geometry.

layer

"all" horizons, or "first": the first horizon(s) of each profile with first_layer_status and profile_markings (see soil_first_layer()). API field layer.

view

"raw": the ISRIC mirror as stored (sent explicitly); "revised": the decided rules of the revised view applied by the API in the response (see soil_revised_rules()). API field view.

profile_type

Profiles by the source's own type term: "synthetic" (KENSOTER), "virtual" (Upper Tana), "none" (no type in the source record), all selecting or all excluded with a "!" prefix (c("!synthetic", "!virtual")); NULL keeps every profile. API field profile_type.

components

Components of multi-component map units (SOTWIS, SOTER polygons): NULL (the API default, "representative"), "representative" (largest proportion_percent), "all", or "cumulative" (by decreasing proportion until min_cumulative_percent). API field components.

min_cumulative_percent

Threshold of components = "cumulative", 0 to 100 (required with it, refused without it). API field min_cumulative_percent.

layout

"wide" (one row per horizon, the default) or "long" (one row per observation). API field layout.

with_geometry

The geometry of each row's feature (EPSG:4326): "none" (the default), "text" (wide: geometry_kind and geometry_text as WKT, sent once per feature by the API; long: geometry_text as GeoJSON, sent on every row) or "sf" (an sf object with a geometry column; needs the package sf, else a soilhub_dependency_error). Rows without geometry (WISE profiles without coordinates) get NA (text) or an empty geometry (sf) and one warning. For polygons prefer the wide layout: the long layout repeats the geometry on every observation. API fields geometry_format (wide) and include_geometry (long).

max_rows

Maximum number of rows to read (Inf: the whole selection). Client-side; caps the API field limit of each page request.

offset

Rows of the selection to skip (to continue a partial read). API field offset (of the first page request).

page_size

Rows per request; NULL uses the session's, the soilhub.page_size option or the server's max_page_size. Client-side; sets the API field limit of each page request.

too_large

What to do when the API refuses the selection as too large for a synchronous read: "stop" raises soilhub_load_limit_error, whose message names the equivalent soil_export() call; "export" exports the same selection (CSV; GeoJSON for the long layout with geometry), waits, downloads it into the export directory, reads it back and returns the same shape as the synchronous read, with soil_metadata(x)$via_export the job id (the whole selection is exported; offset and max_rows select its rows). Client-side: not sent to the API.

progress

Report the pages read (messages at verbosity 1 or more). Client-side: not sent to the API.

timeout

Seconds allowed for each page request; NULL uses the session's (300 s by default). Client-side: not sent to the API.

Value

A soil_table (see soil_table): a data frame (an sf object with with_geometry = "sf") with the attributes soil_metadata (see soil_metadata()) and soil_layout ("wide" or "long").

Details

Terms: a feature is where a profile or map unit is (feature_id); a profile a described soil profile (SOTER PRID); a component a soil component of a multi-component map unit (SOTWIS and SOTER polygons; component_rank is the SOTER SCID); a horizon a layer of a profile (SOTER HONU); an observation one measured value. A wide row is one horizon of one feature and component: its key is dataset, feature_id, component_id, horizon_id (a SOTER horizon appears once per polygon component linked to its profile).

Columns (design 5.2), in the API's order: the fixed columns (dataset, provider_code, feature_id, profile_id, component_id, component_rank integer, horizon_id, horizon_name, upper_depth_cm, lower_depth_cm double, source_support, release_code); with layer = "first" first_layer_status and profile_markings (list of character); the component columns when SOTWIS or SOTER polygons are selected (proportion_percent, cumulative_proportion_percent, terrain_proportion_percent double, is_representative, profile_inside_polygon logical, suid, tcid, scid integer, the others character); the source columns source_profile_type (SOTER: synthetic, virtual), source_record_note, profile_attr_<key> and horizon_attr_<key> (verbatim text: horizon_attr_organic_surface is "true"/"false" as served); the raw markings (texture_sum double, consistency_flags and also_in_datasets lists of character, possible_profile, superseded_by, cell_markings a list of named lists: variable column -> markings); value_flags (list of named lists: variable column -> flags, NULL where none); retired_in_release (the release in which the row's source left ISRIC, still served) and retired_cells (named character: the cells retired while the row is not); with view = "revised" revised_markings (named lists: horizon markings, hidden_values a data frame property_code, rule, source_value, and cells); with with_geometry = "text" geometry_kind and geometry_text (WKT, EPSG:4326, the geometry of the row's feature); then, sorted by name, one group per variable: <key> (double when the column is numeric on every page, else the original text), <key>_units, <key>_method (the laboratory method code of the value), <key>_n (integer: measurements collapsed into the cell, the first by ingestion order is kept) and, for columns with multi-value cells, <key>_values. <key> is the canonical property key (organic_carbon); source codes without a canonical mapping are src_<code>. With with_geometry = "sf" the result is an sf object whose geometry column replaces geometry_text.

Long layout (design 5.3): one row per observation, the columns of the API's ObservationRecord in its order: dataset, observation_id, feature_id, component_id, component_rank (integer), horizon_id, horizon_name, upper_depth_cm, lower_depth_cm (double), property_code (the source code, ORGC), value (double: the number the API extracted from the source value), value_raw (list: the source value verbatim, a number, a string or a list of strings), unit, provider_code, release_code, release_id (integer), canonical_feature_id, canonical_horizon_id, canonical_property_key (organic_carbon), source_support, lineage (list), geometry_kind; the laboratory method (method_code, method_description, method_tension_kpa); the source descriptors profile_attributes, horizon_attributes, component_attributes (lists), source_profile_type, source_record_note; the raw markings of the cell (value_count integer, methods_differ logical, value_spread double, source_method_kind list of character, method_facets list), of the layer (texture_sum, consistency_flags) and of the profile (also_in_datasets, possible_profile, superseded_by); value_flags (list of character); retired_in_release; with view = "revised" revised_markings (named lists, hidden_values a data frame); with layer = "first" first_layer_status and profile_markings; the component columns when SOTWIS or SOTER polygons are selected. Fields the API sends only for some selections are present only then. soil_metadata(x)$total_count is the exact number of observations of the selection (the long layout counts it on every page).

The wide and the long layout of the same selection hold the same horizons (keys dataset, feature_id, component_id, horizon_id); the wide <key> is the first long value of that property by ingestion order and <key>_n the number of long rows of it.

Multi-value cells. About 6 % of the WoSIS measurements hold several values in one cell (a JSON list of 2 to 10 values); the API returns the list as text. <key> receives the mean of the listed values (the value WoSIS publishes; NA when an element is not a number) and <key>_values every original value verbatim (character; NULL for the single-value cells); soil_metadata(x)$multi_value_rule is "mean" and soil_columns() counts the multi-value cells. The other markings of the cell (value_count, methods_differ, value_spread, source_method_kind, method_facets) are in cell_markings. In the long layout the API extracts no number from such a cell: value receives the same mean, computed by the client, and value_raw keeps the listed values.

Pages. The API returns at most max_page_size horizons per request (1000; see soil_capabilities()); the pages are read until the selection is exhausted or max_rows rows are read, and their columns are aligned (a variable absent from a page is NA there). A failure after some pages raises the error with the rows already read in e$partial (a soil_table whose metadata has complete = FALSE and next_offset): continue with offset = soil_metadata(e$partial)$next_offset.

Large selections. The API refuses a synchronous read above its limit (limits$max_sync_observations, 1,000,000 observations today) with soilhub_load_limit_error; its message prints the soil_export() call of the same selection; too_large = "export" exports it and reads it back. Run soil_summary() first to size a selection.

Rights: soil:read. Capabilities: revised_view for view = "revised", profile_type_filter for profile_type, component_selection for components, observation_geometry for the geometry of the long layout.

See also

soil_features(), soil_columns(), soil_flags(), soil_markings(), soil_revised_rules(), soil_first_layer(), soil_citations()

Other reads: soil_features()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
soil <- soil_connect()
x <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "KEN",
                       variables = c("organic_carbon", "clay"), max_rows = 100)
x
soil_columns(x)
soil_citations(x)

# first horizons of SOTER, revised view
y <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "soter_profiles", layer = "first",
                       view = "revised", country = "KEN")
table(y$first_layer_status)
soil_revised_rules(y)

# a refused selection names the export call
tryCatch(soil_observations(soil), soilhub_load_limit_error = function(e) e)

# one row per observation, with the geometry as sf
z <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "KEN",
                       variables = "organic_carbon", layout = "long",
                       with_geometry = "sf", max_rows = 100)
soil_metadata(z)$total_count
} # }
